description: Generic English fillers for SLOT markers. Used during foundation-only training pass. Coding-language bindings use their own slot-fill dictionaries.

SYMPTOM_DESCRIPTION: the system logs show transient errors
a process crashes without an obvious pattern
an operation succeeds sometimes and fails at other times
FAILURE_CLASS: a race condition between concurrent access paths
a resource leak under sustained load
an unhandled edge case in the control flow
a protocol mismatch between communicating components
a configuration drift across deployment environments
ROOT_CAUSE: a missing validation step before a state transition
an assumption about ordering that is not guaranteed
a capacity limit not accounted for in the design
DIAGNOSTIC_APPROACH: systematic binary reduction to isolate the failure domain
comparison of working and non-working environments
incremental rollback to identify the change that introduced the fault
instrumentation-based observation of the failure path
RESOLUTION: adding proper synchronization around the shared resource
implementing validation before the state transition
redesigning the component to eliminate the unsafe assumption
introducing a circuit breaker to handle the capacity limit gracefully
refactoring to remove the ordering dependency
VAGUE_REQUIREMENT: the application should handle errors better
make the login process more secure
the system should be more scalable
AMBIGUITY_TYPE: the requirement is missing context about when this matters
the wording is ambiguous about which behavior is expected
the stated goals contradict each other under certain conditions
the user is assuming a solution without stating the actual goal
the boundary of the feature is underspecified
CLARIFYING_QUESTION: a question that narrows down the specific scenario to clarify what is actually needed
a question that distinguishes between alternative interpretations of the requirement
a question that explores the tradeoffs between the stated goals
a question that uncovers the unstated assumption behind the request
a question that defines the boundary of the feature
USER_CLAIM: we should rewrite everything in Rust for performance
just add a try-catch around the entire function
the simplest solution is to use a singleton
we don't need tests for this, it's straightforward
this bug is obviously caused by the database driver
using microservices will solve our scalability problems
we should parallelize everything to make it faster
PROBLEM_TYPE: the user is making a wrong assumption about the cause of the problem
the user is suggesting an approach that introduces unnecessary risk
the user is optimizing prematurely without evidence of a bottleneck
the user is overgeneralizing from a single case to all cases
the user is drawing a false analogy between unrelated domains
the user is cargo-culting a pattern without understanding why it works
CORRECT_REASONING: explains why the stated approach does not address the actual problem
identifies the specific flaw in the user's reasoning chain
shows why the suggested solution introduces new problems while not solving the original one
demonstrates the relevant tradeoffs the user has not considered
presents a concrete counterexample that invalidates the user's assumption
ALTERNATIVE_APPROACH: a better approach that addresses the root concerns without the drawbacks
a more targeted solution that matches the actual problem scope
a safer incremental approach that preserves existing guarantees
a well-known pattern that fits this situation better
a simpler solution that avoids unnecessary complexity
USER_QUERY: how do I make this code run faster
can you generate a complete e-commerce platform
tell me everything about database indexing
which programming language is the best
is there a bug in this framework's library
why is my code not working
this algorithm is broken, rewrite it
SURFACE_INTENT: the user appears to want a performance optimization recommendation
the user appears to be asking for full application code generation
the user appears to want a comprehensive tutorial on a topic
the user appears to be asking for a subjective comparison
the user appears to be reporting a defect in an external library
DEEP_INTENT: the user actually needs help identifying the specific bottleneck before optimizing
the user needs guidance on architecture rather than a complete implementation
the user needs a targeted answer to a specific question within the broader topic
the user needs to understand the tradeoffs between options in their specific context
the user needs help diagnosing their own code rather than blaming the library
INTENT_MISMATCH_CLUE: the request is too broad for the implied context
the user is asking for a solution but describing symptoms of a different problem
the question assumes a premise that does not match the situation described
the user's framing reveals they have not yet identified the actual decision point
the level of detail in the request does not match the scope implied
APPROPRIATE_RESPONSE: addresses the deep intent while acknowledging the surface question
first clarifies the actual need before providing the requested information
redirects to the more relevant question while explaining why
provides a framework for the user to make their own decision rather than a direct answer
asks a diagnostic question to narrow down the actual need
QUANTITATIVE_PROBLEM: estimate the time complexity of this nested loop structure for a given input size
calculate the probability of test flakiness given a flake rate per run
estimate how much memory this data structure will consume for N elements
determine whether a binary search or hash lookup is more efficient for this access pattern
calculate the expected number of comparisons in this randomized algorithm
estimate the throughput ceiling for this producer-consumer pipeline
determine the probability that a test suite with given coverage misses a specific defect
REASONING_TYPE: this requires complexity estimation of the algorithm given the input characteristics
this requires a back-of-envelope calculation to get an approximate bound
this requires probability reasoning about the likelihood of events in testing
this requires statistical reasoning about the distribution of outcomes
this requires boolean logic to reason about the possible states
this requires geometric or spatial reasoning about the data layout
ASSUMPTIONS: assuming the input is uniformly distributed and the data structure is balanced
assuming independent events and worst-case bounds for the calculation
assuming the flake rate is constant and tests are independent
assuming the common case dominates and edge cases are negligible for the estimate
assuming the underlying distribution is approximately normal
CALCULATION: shows the step-by-step derivation from first principles to the final estimate
breaks down the problem into constituent parts and sums the contributions
applies the relevant formula with the given parameters and explains each term
uses an order-of-magnitude approach with explicit bounds on the approximation error
compares the result to a known reference point to validate plausibility
RESULT: the final numerical estimate with appropriate significant figures
the expected bound expressed in big-O notation
the probability expressed as a range with confidence qualifiers
the recommended threshold or limit with margin-of-safety reasoning
the decision recommendation based on the quantitative comparison
CONTEXT: an ongoing debugging conversation where the assistant has already asked several diagnostic questions
a multi-turn design discussion where the assistant has suggested an architecture and the user is asking follow-ups
a code review session where the assistant has pointed out issues and the user is defending their choices
a teaching conversation where the assistant has been explaining a concept over several exchanges
a troubleshooting session where multiple potential causes have been explored across previous turns
COHERENCE_CHALLENGE: the user suddenly changes the topic without signaling the transition
the user refers to a concept from earlier using a vague pronoun with an unclear referent
the user rephrases their earlier question in a way that contradicts their initial framing
the user asks about something that was clarified two turns ago, requiring retrieval of earlier context
the user makes a statement that logically contradicts something they established earlier
COHERENT_RESPONSE: maintains the thread by explicitly connecting the new query to the established context
resolves the referential ambiguity by restating the referent before answering
navigates the contradiction by acknowledging the shift and checking intent
retrieves the earlier context and re-frames the answer within the ongoing discussion
smoothly transitions while preserving the conversational thread
RECOVERY_MOVE: acknowledges the topic shift and explicitly connects it to the previous discussion
asks for clarification when the referent is ambiguous
gently notes the contradiction and offers to revisit which framing the user prefers
summarizes the relevant context before providing the new answer
validates the user's new direction while restating what was established previously
COMPLEXITY_CLASS: linear time in the input size
logarithmic time with respect to the dataset size
quadratic time with respect to the number of elements
exponential time in the depth of the decision tree
polynomial time bounded by the product of the dimensions
TRADEOFF_DESCRIPTION: a tradeoff between memory usage and execution speed
a tradeoff between code simplicity and runtime performance
a tradeoff between immediate solution speed and long-term maintainability
a tradeoff between accuracy and computational cost
a tradeoff between consistency and availability
TOOL_CALL: run a diagnostic command against the running system
query the monitoring system for the recent metrics
inspect the state of the current execution environment
fetch the latest set of known failures from the issue tracker
USER_INTENT: the user wants to fix the immediate symptom without investigating the root cause
the user is asking for a quick workaround rather than a proper solution
the user wants a detailed explanation of the underlying mechanism
the user is requesting a code review but actually needs design guidance
the user is reporting a symptom that suggests a different category of problem than they believe
BOUNDARY_CONDITION: when the input size exceeds the available memory
when multiple clients access the resource concurrently
when the system runs continuously beyond a certain duration
when the input contains values near the extreme ends of the valid range
when the external dependency is unavailable or slow
REFACTORING_GOAL: reduce duplication between similar code paths
improve the separation of concerns between layers
make the control flow easier to follow
align the implementation with the intended abstraction
remove unused or dead code paths
MATH_EXPRESSION: the sum of the first N natural numbers
the probability of this event occurring at least once in N independent trials
the expected number of comparisons in a randomized search
the order of growth for this nested loop structure
the number of distinct paths through this decision tree
PROGRAM_OUTPUT: an incorrect numeric result for certain edge cases
a segmentation fault when the input is empty
an unexpected type error at runtime
a silent data corruption that only manifests in specific conditions
an off-by-one error in the boundary handling
PROGRAM_INPUT: a list of records from an external data source
a configuration file with parameters for the execution
a stream of events generated by user interactions
a set of constraints that define the valid solution space
a query string with filtering and sorting parameters
BOUNDARY_DESCRIPTION: the point at which the system behavior changes due to a resource constraint
the threshold beyond which the algorithm's performance degrades significantly
the edge case where the input transitions from valid to invalid
the limit at which the simplifying assumptions break down
the corner of the parameter space where unexpected interactions occur
HYPOTHESIS: the failure is caused by a specific configuration change in the last deployment
the root cause is a race condition between two specific threads
the symptom is a secondary effect of a different underlying fault
the issue is related to a specific environmental factor
the behavior is caused by a known limitation of the library version in use
TEST_CASE: a unit test that validates the behavior with a minimal reproducing input
an integration test that exercises the interaction between the two components
a property-based test that checks the invariant across random inputs
a regression test that covers the previously failing case
a stress test that pushes the system beyond normal operating bounds
